findings.title: The displaced command becomes a chosen protection
findings.claim: The authority named in رَبِّهِ is the relation that Iblis leaves and that the focus's human addressees are then asked to reassign to Iblis and his offspring as protective allies.
findings.mechanism: The carrier 18:50:15:1 names the Lord relation through ownership, command authority, and governance; the independent focus triggers 18:50:12:2 and 18:50:18:1 join Iblis's departure from that command to the deliberate taking of him as awliya. The wider connections at 34:12, 72:6, and 17:2 return through the same command, jinn, refuge, and trustee relations, so taking the dissenter as protector reads as a relational repetition of the first refusal.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning becomes more precise than a general prohibition of bad friendship: the alleged protection is an authority arrangement that installs the one who rejected the Lord's command as a substitute source of allegiance.
findings.containment: This adds a qualified relational resonance to the focus's plain warning. It does not equate human and divine authority, make every use of awliya false, or claim that all wider parallels carry the same force; the target connection rows supply Arabic and relation notes but not target morphology.

epistemic.reason: The core focus branch and trusted publication are anchored, while the represented reader-walk support is legacy-unbound and the connection targets lack target morphology.

branch_activations.carrier: رَبِّهِ carries the Lord relation as the authority, ownership, and governing relation attached to Iblis.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The focus pairs Iblis's departure from the command with the deliberate taking of Iblis and his offspring as awliya, while the supplied 34:12, 72:6, and 17:2 connections independently return the command, jinn, refuge, and trustee relations to this focus.
branch_activations.activation: The authority relation carried by رَبِّهِ meets the later protective-alliance act: the relation abandoned in the first scene is selected again as the framework in which the dissenter is trusted. The wider connections make that contact global rather than a merely local word association.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Taking Iblis as an ally becomes a relational repetition of refusal, because the authority displaced by his rebellion is reinstalled as a protective allegiance to him and his line.
branch_activations.boundary: The activation concerns this constructed Rabb relation and the supplied connection traces; it does not generalize the branch to every use of Rabb or identify human authority with divine lordship.

findings.title: The exception emerges from the containing order
findings.claim: The focus's departure can be read analogically as an emergence from a containing order: the completed collective obedience makes the isolated refusal disclose a different orientation.
findings.mechanism: The carrier فَسَقَ at 18:50:12:2 ordinarily names departure or rupture from the command. The independent triggers are the commanded collective's completed prostration, the exception particle, Iblis's isolation, and the supplied parallel scenes at 2:34, 17:61, 20:116, 7:11, and 38:74. Their repeated command-plus-exception structure lets the physical branch image of a taze hurma emerging from its peel color the focus as disclosure through rupture.
findings.reader_payoff: The exception is perceptible as more than a second event after obedience: the collective frame becomes the containing surface from which Iblis's different orientation suddenly shows itself.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory analogy that supports the plain account of disobedience. The focus does not grammatically make the command a shell, and فَسَقَ is not being lexically replaced by the taze hurma meaning; the retained image is limited to the inside/outside relation and the focus's exception structure.

epistemic.reason: The reader-walk nomination is legacy-unbound and the connection rows supply target Arabic without target morphology; the exact focus carrier, branch facet, and structural triggers are nevertheless present.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The completed collective prostration, the exception particle, Iblis's proper-name isolation, the explanatory classification clause, and five supplied parallel prostration scenes independently repeat the containing-order/exception relation.
branch_activations.activation: The physical branch image contributes only its relation of an inside object emerging through its enclosing peel. branch_activations.resulting_reading: Iblis's departure exposes the orientation that the apparent collective obedience had concealed: the exception emerges from the order and makes its difference visible.
branch_activations.boundary: The activation is analogical and exploratory. It makes no claim that amr literally means shell, that the focus concerns dates, or that the physical branch is the lexical gloss of فَسَقَ here.

findings.title: The primordial warning returns as a closing danger
findings.claim: The focus's warning about taking Iblis and his offspring as awliya returns at 18:102 and is given an exclusive Lord-directed endpoint at 18:110, making the primordial refusal a continuing relational danger within the supplied surah frame.
findings.mechanism: The retrospective support names the two later returns, and the reciprocal connection records identify 18:102 as a direct condemnation of taking Iblis and his offspring as allies and 18:110 as the closing prohibition of associating another in the Lord's worship. The focus's taking-and-allegiance act is therefore reopened by later same-surah relations rather than left as a closed origin scene.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's final question is newly perceptible as a danger that the surah itself revisits: the bad exchange remains active wherever a substitute protector is installed beside the Lord.
findings.containment: This is a same-surah beyond-pericope resonance grounded in the two supplied connection rows and the attributed retrospective. It does not state the surah's full thesis, rank these later verses over the focus, or replace the focus's local narrative and rebuke.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective source is legacy-unbound, while both same-surah connection records explicitly return to the focus; the packet supplies target Arabic but not target morphology.

findings.title: The ally relation becomes a failed protection exchange
findings.claim: The focus installs those it has named as enemies in a near-supporting ally role, while the wider supplied relations make the final badal an exchange whose promised protection is exposed as disavowal and failure.
findings.mechanism: The awliya carrier at 18:50:18:1 meets the independent enemy predicate at 18:50:23:1 and the supplied 35:6, 8:48, 14:22, and 59:16 connections, where Satan is opposed as enemy, promises or receives allegiance, and then lacks authority or disowns the follower. The badal carrier at 18:50:26:1 meets the same taking, exclusion, and enemy relations, so the closing exchange becomes an operational substitution of failed protection for the Lord-directed relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why friendship, protection, and exchange belong to one movement here: the error is a practical support arrangement that treats an avowed enemy as a dependable ally, then discovers that the promised support cannot answer.
findings.containment: The connection targets provide exact Arabic and authored relation notes but no target morphology, so this remains a qualified global resonance. It applies to the focus's Iblis-and-offspring relation and the supplied Satan parallels; it does not universalize the failure to every alliance or every use of the two branches.

epistemic.reason: The branch carriers and focus morphology are supplied, while the global triggers are connection records whose target morphology is explicitly absent and whose prior labels are not decisions.
